'''Jimena Canales''' (born 1973) is a Mexican-American historian of science and author with a background in physics and engineering.

==Career==
Jimena Canales is the author of ''Simply Einstein'' (2021),<ref>{{cite book|isbn=978-1943657452|title=Simply Einstein|last1=Canales|first1=Jimena|date=14 March 2021}}</ref> ''Bedeviled: A Shadow History of Demons in Science'' (2020),<ref>{{cite book|url=https://press.princeton.edu/books/hardcover/9780691175324/bedeviled|title = Bedeviled: A Shadow History of Demons in Science| date=10 November 2020 | isbn=9780691175324 | last1=Canales | first1=Jimena }}</ref> ''The Physicist and the Philosopher: Einstein, Bergson and the Debate that Changed Our Understanding of Time'' (2015)<ref>{{cite book|url=http://press.princeton.edu/titles/10445.html| title = The Physicist and the Philosopher: Einstein, Bergson and the Debate that Changed Our Understanding of Time| date = 4 October 2016| isbn = 9780691173177| last1 = Canales| first1 = Jimena}}</ref> and ''A Tenth of a Second: A History'' (2009)<ref name="uchicago.edu">{{cite book|url=https://press.uchicago.edu/ucp/books/book/chicago/T/bo6922088.html|title = A Tenth of a Second| publisher=University of Chicago Press |via=press.uchicago.edu}}</ref> as well as numerous articles on the history of modernity; specializing in art, science and technology (appearing in [[Artforum]], [[Aperture (magazine)|Aperture]], [[Wired (magazine)|WIRED]], [[The New Yorker]],<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.newyorker.com/tech/annals-of-technology/albert-einsteins-sci-fi-stories|title=Albert Einstein's Sci-Fi Stories|first=Jimena|last=Canales|magazine=The New Yorker}}</ref> [[The Atlantic]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theatlantic.com/science/archive/2017/04/atom-bomb-pr/523413/|title=The Secret PR Push That Shaped the Atomic Bomb's Origin Story|first=Jimena|last=Canales|date=April 18, 2017|website=The Atlantic}}</ref> [[NPR]],<ref>NPR [https://www.npr.org/sections/13.7/2018/01/09/575072389/siri-cortana-and-alexa-carry-the-marks-of-their-human-makers 2018/01/09], [https://www.npr.org/sections/13.7/2018/01/15/575072170/darwin-s-shopping-list 2018/01/15], [https://www.npr.org/sections/13.7/2018/03/13/593140019/an-ode-to-insignificance-buttons-touchscreens-and-other-dangerous-technologies 2018/03/13]</ref> among others).
Canales obtained a B.S. in engineering physics at the [[Instituto Tecnológico de Estudios Superiores de Monterrey]] in 1995, a master's degree in History of Science at the [[Harvard University]] and a PhD in History of Science at the same university in 2003. In 2004 she worked as an assistant professor in the Department of History of Science at [[Harvard University]] and in 2013 she was promoted to [[associate professor]].<ref>https://www.thecrimson.com/article/2004/5/12/history-of-science-reinvents-tutorials-the/. http://www.thecrimson.com/column/bargain-hunting-fall-2010/article/2010/9/5/class-science-title-professors/ {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150602083951/http://www.thecrimson.com/column/bargain-hunting-fall-2010/article/2010/9/5/class-science-title-professors/ |date=2015-06-02 }}. http://www.thecrimson.com/article/2010/11/2/music-sound-timbre-sheldon/</ref> In 2012 she was senior fellow at the [[Internationales Kolleg für Kulturtechnikforschung und Medienphilosophie]] and in the summer she worked as a [[Visiting scholar|visiting professor]] at the Summer School for Media Studies at [[Princeton University]] in the German department.<ref>http://www.ikkm-weimar.de/en/fellows/former-fellows/jimena-canales/ {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402133404/http://www.ikkm-weimar.de/en/fellows/former-fellows/jimena-canales/ |date=2015-04-02 }}. http://german.princeton.edu/ssms/academic-staff-2/academic-staff-2012/jimena-canales/ {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160310185323/http://german.princeton.edu/ssms/academic-staff-2/academic-staff-2012/jimena-canales/ |date=2016-03-10 }}</ref> In 2013 she was recruited to the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]] as the Thomas M. Siebel Chair in the History of Science, which she held until 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://finance.yahoo.com/news/siebel-chair-history-science-illinois-203000632.html |title=Siebel Chair in the History of Science at Illinois Named - Yahoo Finance |accessdate=2017-01-15 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402141743/http://finance.yahoo.com/news/siebel-chair-history-science-illinois-203000632.html |archivedate=2015-04-02 }}. http://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20141030006706/en/Siebel-Chair-History-Science-Illinois-Named#.VQ4gSMaRk7A. {{cite web |url=http://www.history.illinois.edu/news/newsletters/documents/HistoryNewsletter2014.pdf |title=Archived copy |accessdate=2015-05-04 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402174642/http://www.history.illinois.edu/news/newsletters/documents/HistoryNewsletter2014.pdf |archivedate=2015-04-02 }}. http://www.trustees.uillinois.edu/trustees/agenda/November-14-2013/003-nov-Appointments.pdf</ref>

Jimena Canales has collaborated with the philosopher [[Bruno Latour]], the artist [[Olafur Eliasson]] and the cosmologist [[Lee Smolin]].<ref>http://www.e-flux.com/journal/some-experiments-in-art-and-politics/ {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150502194723/http://www.e-flux.com/journal/some-experiments-in-art-and-politics/ |date=2015-05-02 }}. {{cite web |url=http://futurenows.net/entry/institut-fur-raumexperimente/ |title=Festival of Future Nows &#124; Institut für Raumexperimente |accessdate=2015-05-04 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20150324074646/http://futurenows.net/entry/institut-fur-raumexperimente/ |archivedate=2015-03-24 }}</ref>

Her presentations on art and science has been featured at the [[Centre Georges Pompidou]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.e-flux.com/journal/23/67790/some-experiments-in-art-and-politics/|title=Some Experiments in Art and Politics - Journal #23 March 2011 - e-flux|website=www.e-flux.com}}</ref> [[San Francisco Museum of Modern Art]] (SFMOMA),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sfmoma.org/read/photographic-event-2016/|title=The Photographic Event · SFMOMA|website=www.sfmoma.org}}</ref> the 11th [[Shanghai Biennale]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.e-flux.com/announcements/61969/why-not-ask-again-arguments-counter-arguments-and-stories/|title=Why Not Ask Again: Arguments, Counter-arguments, and Stories - Announcements - e-flux|website=www.e-flux.com}}</ref> and the [[Institute of Contemporary Art, Boston]] (ICA).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icaboston.org/events/artist%E2%80%99s-voice-trevor-paglen-and-jimena-canales|title=The Artist's Voice: Trevor Paglen and Jimena Canales &#124; icaboston.org|website=www.icaboston.org}}</ref>
